newsitem.title: USA: Whitehall says Air Force cancels contract.
newsitem.headline: Whitehall says Air Force cancels contract.

text.p: Whitehall Corp said on Wednesday that the U.S. Air Force terminated its maintenance contract with Whitehall's wholly owned subsidiary, Aero Corp.
Whitehall said in a news release that the Air Force cancelled the C-130 aircraft maintenance agreement because it decided to have C-130 work done at an Air Force facility this year.
The contract, awarded in April, was to be for a year, with optional renewals. Over five years it would have been worth $100 million.
The company said Aero will be compensated for the costs it incurred in connection with the contract.
A Whitehall spokesman said the company derives most of its revenues from Aero.
Whitehall said it believes the Air Force will recontract the C-130 work in early 1998, and the company intends to bid for it again.
"We believe we can secure enough commercial maintenance work for the remainder of 1997 to offset the revenues from the C-130 contract," Whitehall Chairman George Baker said.
The company also announced that it agreed to buy the aircraft maintenance operation of privately held Zantop International Airlines Inc, located at Middle Georgia Regional Airport in Macon, Ga.
This operation has annual revenues of $20 million, Whitehall said. Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed.
Whitehall, through Aero, rebuilds, modifies and maintains commercial and military aircraft.
